title: Validating LLM-Generated Synthetic Survey Samples: A Use-Dependent Multi-Dimensional Framework for Social-Science Applications
abstract: arXiv:2611.00256v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) make it increasingly feasible to generate synthetic survey respondents, but their empirical usefulness cannot be judged by a single notion of accuracy. A synthetic sample may perform weakly at the respondent level while still preserving distributional or substantive relationships relevant to social-science analysis. We develop a use-dependent, multi-dimensional validation framework distinguishing predictive, distributional, and substantive validity, and illustrate it using Eurobarometer data on attitudes toward artificial intelligence. Four off-the-shelf LLMs generate responses conditional on observed respondent profiles, while supervised machine learning provides a predictive reference for interpreting their performance. translated_title: 验证大语言模型生成的合成调查样本：一种面向社会科学应用的基于用途的多维框架
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）使生成合成调查受访者变得越来越可行，但其实证有用性无法通过单一的准确性概念来评判。一个合成样本可能在受访者个体层面表现较弱，却仍能保留与社会科学分析相关的分布性或实质性关系。我们开发了一个基于用途的多维验证框架，区分预测有效性、分布有效性和实质有效性，并以关于人工智能态度的欧洲晴雨表（Eurobarometer）数据为例加以说明。四个现成的大语言模型在给定观察到的受访者特征的条件下生成回答，同时利用监督式机器学习提供预测参考基准来解释其表现。结果显示各验证维度之间存在实质性差异：一些大语言模型生成的样本能够保留有意义的边际异质性、人口统计排序、跨国差异……
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于用途的多维验证框架，从预测、分布和实质三个维度评估大语言模型生成的合成调查样本在社会科学研究中的有效性，并以欧洲晴雨表人工智能态度数据为例展示了不同模型在各维度上的表现差异。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a use-dependent, multi-dimensional validation framework—distinguishing predictive, distributional, and substantive validity—to assess LLM-generated synthetic survey samples for social-science applications, illustrated with Eurobarometer data on attitudes toward artificial intelligence.
